items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: One in particular, Mr. Lavenneu, conducted the orchestra... But we loved him, we loved him. We knew that he knew and he was directing us in the right way.

ctx.x: Did you grow up listening to the kind of music that you eventually played? Radio? No?

No. We started, my grandfather was an opera buff and liked classical music, symphonic music, and that’s what we listened to first and that’s what I played first. And I was fairly good at it and played in a junior symphony in Philadelphia and Symphony Club in Philadelphia, as I was twelve, eight, eight to twelve years old playing in that. And then I took a music course at the vocational school, Mastbaum in Philadelphia. In fact Joe Wilder was here with us — Joe Wilder? He and I were in the same class together back…
Yeah. He cared enough to get angry I guess.
